title: Run the four test suites again so each result records which version it tested
ask: The stored suite results predate the change that made runs stamp the commit they proved, so their age is unknowable rather than large. Re-run the four suites from the Engineering page so each stamps a commit, then confirm the freshness column reads a number instead of 'unknown'.
first_action: Press Run on each of the four suites on #/pillar/engineering and watch the 'how far behind main' column.
source_message: The stored suite results predate the change that made runs stamp the commit they proved, so their age is unknowable rather than large. Re-run the four suites from the Engineering page so each stamps a commit, then confirm the freshness column reads a number instead of 'unknown'.
result:
Ran all four suites — unit, integration, robot session, sim benchmark — from the live Engineering page's Run buttons. All four passed and each now stamps `4b20852` (main's current tip) as the commit it proved. The "how far behind main" column reads 0 commits for every row, and the freshness goal shows "4 of 4 hold," green.

No code change was needed. The commit-stamping logic was already in place from the earlier fix; the stored results were just old runs from before that logic existed, so they had no commit to check against. Re-running them was the whole fix — the worktree is clean, nothing to diff.

Nothing else to flag: the suites themselves are green, and the freshness reading now resolves cleanly for all four.

check.summary: All four suites were re-run at 09:20 today and each stored result stamps 4b20852, the current tip of main, so the freshness column now reads 0 commits behind for every row; the empty diff is correct because run results live in the gitignored hq/data/runs/ on the desktop, so there was nothing to commit. Watch the sim benchmark: it cleared its 100,000x gate at 103,810x, a margin under 4% that a busy machine could flip red.

changed.title: Re-run the suites so each stamps the commit it proved

amendments.why: Reworded in plain language: the old title used words that mean something precise inside this studio and nothing outside it.
